step1.title: WALL CONFIGURATION
step1.subtitle: Step 1/3 · House structure (set once)
step1.sillHint: 💡 Leave empty or enter 0 if no sill will be installed (garage door, certain sliding doors, sill-less renovation).
step1.horizontalCutSub: Presence of a horizontal stop return
step1.allegeHint: 💡 The 'Sill height' option is now entered per opening (Measurements step), as it may vary from one bay to another.

step2.title: WINDOW SELECTION
step2.subtitle: Step 2/3 · Choose the exact shape of the window
step2.helperText: The opening type (Fixed, Casement, Tilt-and-turn, Sliding) will be defined in the workshop via the label / reference entered in the next step.
step2.hint: Select the shape that best matches your window. For a polygon (triangle, pentagon, hexagon, octagon), choose « POLYGON » then specify the number of edges.

step3.title: MEASUREMENTS
step3.subtitle: Step 3/3 · {{shape}}
step3.guideHint: ↑ Identify the dimensions to measure on the diagram, then fill them in below.
step3.labelFieldPlaceholder: e.g. Living room, Bedroom 1, Front door, Ref. F-001...
step3.labelFieldHint: ⚠ Provide a label / reference to identify this window.
step3.garageHint: 📏 Specific measurements for a sectional door installation: the lintel is the headroom above the bay; the jambs are the width of solid wall available on either side of the bay to fix the vertical rails (minimum 100 mm recommended).
step3.rulePleinCintre: ✓ Rule: H2 = H1 + L/2 (the top of the half-circle exceeds the sill by L/2).
step3.ruleArcSurbaisse: ✓ Rule: H2 must be > H1 and the rise (H2 − H1) must be < L/2.
step3.helpPleinCintre: ⭕ Full arch — Half-circle arch at the top. Left and right heights are identical.
step3.helpArcSurbaisse: 🌗 Segmental arch — Flattened arch (lower than a half-circle). Left and right heights are identical.
step3.helpAngle90: ◣ Cut corner — Window with one (or two) corner(s) cut at an angle. The orange hatched area on the diagram indicates the cut.
step3.ruleAngle90: ✓ Rule: The cut must be < frame dimensions. The angle is generally 135° (45° oblique), but adjustable based on your measurement.
step3.bowFeedbackText:
Feel free to send us your ideas or measuring techniques to complete this module.

How can we improve the Bow-Window function? How can we make it easier for you by sharing your expertise in choosing measurements?
step3.bowSendButton: SEND YOUR FEEDBACK / EXPERTISE TO THE ADMINISTRATOR
step3.bowDisabled: ⓘ The input form is temporarily disabled. Choose another shape in the previous step, or go back.
step3.helpPentagone: ⬠ Pentagon — Pointed-roof shape (rectangle + triangle on top). H1 = vertical side height; H2 = total height at the peak.
step3.helpHexagone: ⬡ Hexagon — Shape with top AND bottom cut (6 sides).
step3.ruleHexagone: ✓ Rules: Top width < Base width; Sides height < Total height.
step3.helpOvale: ⬭ Oval — Ellipsoidal shape. Enter only total width and total height.
step3.helpPolygone: ⬡ Polygon — Choose the number of edges, then fill in the length of each edge and the angle of each vertex. Default values correspond to a regular polygon.
step3.rulePolygone: ✓ For a regular polygon: all sides have the same length and all vertices have the same angle. For an irregular polygon, enter the average value or contact the technician to fill in each edge separately.
step3.feuillureHint: Measure the bay rebates according to your masonry's specifics.
step3.feuillureCircularHint: The rebate of an oculus is circular and identical all around. A single measurement is enough.
step3.breastworkSub: Masonry below the bay (varies between openings)
step3.mark1mSub: Enables automatic calculation via raw measurement
